title: Automated 3D Pre-Training for Molecular Property Prediction

problem.claim: Molecular property prediction is important in drug discovery and materials science, and geometric structures are necessary for accurate prediction.

gap.claim: Obtaining molecular geometric structures is infeasible in many real-world applications because of high computational cost.

contributions.claim: A 3D pre-training framework called 3D PGT pre-trains a model on 3D molecular graphs and fine-tunes it on molecular graphs without 3D structures.
A multi-task generative pre-training framework uses bond length, bond angle, and dihedral angle as geometric descriptors.
A surrogate metric based on total energy automatically searches for the weight distribution among the three generative pretext tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose a novel 3D pre-training framework named 3D PGT.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on 2D molecular graphs comparing 3D PGT with various pre-training baselines.
The authors report that 3D PGT demonstrates accuracy, efficiency, and generalization ability in those experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Molecular property prediction is important, and geometric structures support prediction performance.
Obtaining molecular geometric structures can be computationally infeasible in real-world applications.
The proposed 3D PGT pre-trains on 3D molecular graphs and fine-tunes without 3D structures.
The framework generates three geometric attributes and uses total energy to automate their task-weight distribution.
Experiments on 2D molecular graphs compare 3D PGT with pre-training baselines and report accuracy, efficiency, and generalization results.

source_observation.claim: The framework transfers pre-training from 3D molecular graphs to downstream molecular graphs without 3D structures.

interpretation.claim: Pre-training can use information-rich representations that are unavailable during downstream inference.

application.claim: When deployment lacks costly geometric inputs, consider pre-training with those inputs and fine-tuning a model that does not require them.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when this transfer strategy fails or what downstream conditions are required.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, quantitative results, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not provide computational cost measurements or details of the total-energy metric.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
